thread:
Alex: Heads-up — ran a quick perf sweep on Flash variants with paged fallback enabled. Results look... surprising. Tokens/sec drops ~22% on 2k seqs when fallback triggers.

Priya: Ugh. Which fallback path? fused->paged or flash->paged?

Alex: flash -> paged-attn path. Baseline (flash-v2, no fallback) at 2k seq: 14.8k tokens/s. With paged fallback it's 11.6k tokens/s. Also saw KV cache misses spike.

Sam: Do you have the profiler output? especially kernel selection traces and batching stats.

Alex: Pasted the relevant snippet from the profiler:

```
[kernel_select] model:llama2-7b  seq:2048  batch:1  chosen:flash_v2  fallback:init_paged
[exec] flash_v2: 54ms/token-window  paged_attn: 82ms/token-window
[cache] kv_hit_rate: 0.72 -> 0.41 (after fallback)
[batcher] avg_batch_size: 3.1 -> 1.9 (tail effects)
```

Diego: That kv_hit_rate drop is huge. Why would fallback reduce cache locality?

Alex: Hypothesis: paged-attn forces smaller effective prefix chunks so KV entries are evicted earlier or we disable some prefix caching optimization to avoid memory blowup. Also fallback causes uneven worker assignment -> smaller batching.

Priya: Can we reproduce with a synthetic trace that forces fallback but keeps batching steady? e.g., pad requests to keep batcher full.

Sam: I ran a microbenchmark: fixed batch size 8 vs auto-batcher. With fixed batch 8, paged fallback only costs ~8% throughput vs flash. With auto-batcher we saw the 22% hit. So batching collapse is a major factor.

Alex: Thanks Sam. So we have two contributors: kernel perf delta (flash vs paged) and batching collapse. Need to quantify $/M tokens impact for SLOs.

Priya: I crunched the numbers quick using our cost model:
- Baseline flash-v2: 14.8k tok/s -> ~3.2M tokens/hr per GPU. At current infra price that's ~ $1.75 per 1M tokens.
- With fallback (auto-batcher) 11.6k tok/s -> ~2.5M tok/hr -> ~ $2.25 per 1M tokens.
So ~28% increase in $/M tokens.

Diego: That's material. Customers on Dedicated care about $/M. We need mitigations: 1) make paged-attn kernels faster; 2) preserve batching by routing; 3) improved KV caching rules to avoid eviction on fallback.

Alex: I've got a small experiment plan: implement a soft-fallback that keeps prefix chunk size and KV policy consistent, and a "fallback-preserve-batch" flag that holds workers until batch is at least N or timeout.

Sam: Also consider adaptive kernel selection that prefers paged only when expected benefit > threshold. Our selector currently uses per-seq heuristics but not expected batching impact.

Priya: For short-term ops, can we add a routing rule: don't route to paged-enabled nodes unless batch rate < X? Might reduce occurrences.

Diego: Ops question — what's the signal that triggered fallback in the production trace? memory pressure? sequence length > window?

Alex: In that trace fallback triggered due to GPU scratch alloc failing for flash tiled kernels at peak concurrent sequences (OOM guard). So it's a capacity-induced fallback.

Sam: We should log a structured metric: fallback_reason (oom|kernel_not_supported|timeout), pre_fallback_batch_size, post_fallback_batch_size, kv_hit_rate before/after. That will help root-cause across tenants.

Priya: Agreed. Also add $$ impact per-fallback-event estimate (roughly delta_tok_s -> delta_cost). We can bake into the incident response.

Alex: Quick patch I tested: disable premature eviction of KV entries on paged nodes (keep per-request prefix cache sticky for 5s). On a small run that recovered ~40% of the kv_hit_rate drop and improved tokens/sec from 11.6k -> 12.9k (auto-batcher). Still not as good as flash, but $/M impact cut to ~15%.

Diego: Nice. Timeline?

Alex: I'll open a PR for the KV sticky policy and a follow-up issue for kernel perf improvements. Also adding the extra metrics Sam suggested.

Sam: For the kernel perf issue, I can prototype a paged-attn micro-kernel that fuses the page lookup step. Might shave 15-20% off paged latency.

Priya: Great. Can we add a short circ pump doc for support to explain fallback cost and mitigation so CS can communicate to customers?

Diego: Yes, support doc + dashboard alert on "fallback_ratio > 5%" per pool.

infra-bot: Deploy started: rollout/kv-sticky-policy -> canary (3 nodes) by Alex at 2026-03-17T10:22:00Z :rocket:

Alex: Will post numbers once canary finishes. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
